title: Questions for a family member
intro: Ask someone who knows the person well and sees them often, ideally away from the person. Ask about changes compared with how the person used to be.

source.citation: Prince M, et al. Int J Geriatr Psychiatry 2011;26(9):899-907.

licence: Items are from the open-access article above (Creative Commons Attribution 2.5; non-commercial). Confirm permission and obtain a validated local-language version before any real field use.

items.prompt: "Has there been a general decline in their mental functioning?"
"Have you noticed a change in their ability to think and reason?"
"Do they often forget where they have put things?"
"Do they sometimes forget what happened the day before?"
"Do they sometimes forget where they are?"
"Do they have difficulty dressing, such as misplacing buttons or putting clothes on in the wrong order or the wrong way?"
items.guide: If the difficulty is only because of a physical problem (for example arthritis or a weak arm), mark No.
